content:
Using multiple devices with Signal at the same time? This encrypted messaging service is making it easier for users to use the app across different iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, rather than being limited to setting up secondary devices as iPads.

In announcing the simultaneous rollout of Android linking support, Signal stated: "We are also expanding linked device support on iOS, allowing you to link an iPhone to your Signal account, in addition to the iPad support we have continuously offered."

When linking an additional iPhone, users can choose to transfer their complete message history, along with saved media from the past 45 days.

Signal noted that the transfer process uses full end-to-end encryption, employing the same "link-and-sync" technology already used by iPad and desktop devices (including the Signal Mac app).

This expanded support is particularly useful for users who use both a work and personal iPhone, or for those who need to test multiple devices.

This update also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to Apple's Messages ecosystem, where conversations sync seamlessly across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal iOS version 8.22 has begun rolling out gradually on the App Store. Signal has also previously introduced a username feature, allowing users to establish contact without sharing a phone number.
